hint: The image a container descends from.

choices.why: Right: it found `web-old`.
That lists stopped containers, from any image.
Container names are not image names.
Labels are something else; the image is the ancestor.

prompt: To print only container ids, one a line, for another command to consume: `docker ps -___`.
`docker logs --since 1h web | wc -l` printed 0, with the log lines shown above it. Why?
hint: Which stream does Go's `log` write to?

choices.text: `--since 1h` excluded every line older than an hour
choices.why: The lines were printed; they only missed the pipe.

choices.text: Standard error never reached the pipe
choices.why: Right: `2>&1` before the pipe counted 2.
`wc -l` counts newlines, whatever the line holds.
It was the default, and `docker logs` read it.

prompt: Which command prints only the user a container runs as?

choices.why: `ps` has no user column.
That lists processes, with more than the user.
Right: one field, `65532:65532`.
The log says what the program wrote, not the configuration.

prompt: `docker exec web sh` failed with `executable file not found`. What does that mean?
hint: What is in a distroless image?

choices.why: It was running; `exec` reached it.
The error is about the file, not permission.
Without `-it` a shell would start and exit; this one was never found.

choices.text: There is no `sh` in the image

prompt: How did an Alpine container reach `shelf` on `localhost:8080` without any port published to it?

choices.why: Right: same `localhost`, so `wget` reached `shelf` directly.

choices.text: Through port 8080 published on the host
choices.why: It asked `localhost` inside, not the host's port.
Containers each have their own `localhost`.
Alpine includes `wget`; `shelf` was in the other container.

prompt: Match each question to the command that answers it without a shell.

pairs.left: What did it change on disk?
Give me the binary it runs
Does it answer on its own `localhost`?

prompt: `docker diff web` printed nothing. What does that say about `shelf`?

choices.text: The command failed silently, without an error message
choices.why: An empty list is the answer, not a failure.
Right, which a read-only run would also guarantee.

choices.text: It has no writable layer, being distroless
choices.why: Every container has one; this one is simply unchanged.
Nothing is hidden; there was nothing to show.

prompt: `docker volume prune -f` removed nothing; `docker volume prune -af` removed `pgdata`. Why the difference?

choices.why: `-f` only skips the confirmation.

choices.text: `pgdata` was still mounted the first time
choices.why: Its container had been removed before either.

choices.text: `-a` adds named volumes no container uses
choices.why: Right: plain `prune` takes only anonymous ones, since Engine 23.

choices.text: Volumes become prunable only after a delay
choices.why: There is no delay; the rule is about names.

prompt: What does `docker image prune`, without `-a`, remove?

choices.text: Every image that no container is using
choices.why: That is `-a`.

choices.text: Images older than thirty days, by default
choices.why: Age needs a `--filter until=`; it is not the default.
Only `-a` would, and only if nothing used them.
Right: there were none, so 0B.

hint: What on a runner is worth keeping?

choices.why: Right: containers, networks, images and cache, which jobs rebuild anyway.
Volumes are rarely the space on a runner, and a job's data could be in one.
